assumptions: Target process is ordinary FDM using PLA or PETG, a 0.4 mm nozzle, 0.20 mm layers, a level 220 x 220 mm or larger bed, and the authored frame-flat stance.
The deliberately generous 1.2 mm radial rail clearance and 0.45 mm post-side clearance are digital nominal values; they are not claims about every printer's achieved gap.

The object is a desk/hand toy, not a child-safety-rated product. The Make result establishes digital geometry and printability checks only, not a successful physical print, durability, comfort, or meditative feel.

components.form: One connected solid: a 7 mm wide rectangular perimeter frame, a 6 mm wide swept figure-eight base ribbon, a circular 4.4 mm rail, and slender 1.5 mm vertical support posts. Two bridge crowns rise with cosine-eased approaches and leave open negative space beneath.
components.interfaces: The rail is 4.4 mm diameter; each support post is 1.5 mm diameter. The collar window clears the rail radially by 1.2 mm and its 2.4 mm bottom slot clears each post by 0.45 mm per side while retaining 1.0 mm overlap per side against the rail.
components.name: Open braided track and hand frame
components.placement: Printed flat on the XY build plane, with the low rail center at Z = 10.4 mm and alternating bridge centers at Z = 23.8 mm.
components.purpose: Provides the bold graspable boundary, the fully visible branch-free route, two alternating bridge layers, and the small posts that preserve print-in-place capture while allowing the collar slot to pass.

components.form: One extruded squared C/crescent collar with a 12 mm outer span, 6.8 mm inner window, 2.6 mm walls, 3.6 mm axial length, and a 2.4 mm lower post slot.
components.interfaces: The inner window clears the 4.4 mm rail by 1.2 mm radially. Its lower slot passes the 1.5 mm posts but cannot pass the 4.4 mm rail, so release would require breaking a solid rather than finding a hidden gate.
components.name: Captive squared crescent runner
components.placement: Authored around the rail at the far-left home station and printed simultaneously as the assembly's second solid.
components.purpose: Supplies the one-thumb moving object and makes the far-lobe direction reversal easy to see and feel.

concept.intended_interaction: Rest the outer frame on the desk or hold one edge in one hand. Push the squared crescent collar with a thumb along the visible rail. Continue through the first bridge, around the far lobe where its route tangent reverses, through the second alternating bridge, and back home. The same ordered route works in either direction and requires no shaking or separate reset.
concept.signature_decision: Make the impossible-looking exchange structural and legible: use a single periodic centerline with projected crossings at X = -17 mm and X = +17 mm, raise opposite visits to 23.8 mm over a 10.4 mm low rail, and support the rest of the circular 4.4 mm rail from an open figure-eight base ribbon. A squared C-shaped moon collar has a 2.4 mm lower slot that clears the 1.5 mm support posts but is narrower than the rail, providing print-in-place topological capture.
concept.summary: A bold open hand frame holds one completely visible, branch-free braided rail. A print-in-place crescent collar remains permanently captive as it follows two separated alternating over-under bridges; its travel direction reverses at the far lobe and returns at home, so the orientation event is visible without a gate, loose part, or reset gesture.
concept.title: Eclipse Braid
unresolved_risks: A physical print is still required to learn breakaway friction, layer-direction wear, and whether the collar moves smoothly over every post transition.

The support-free bridge geometry and nominal clearances pass deterministic CAD and mesh checks, but printer cooling, extrusion calibration, and material shrinkage can change real bridge sag and running friction.
Human evaluation is needed before describing the interaction as comfortable or meditative; this Make stage only supports the intended one-handed continuous interaction.

deterministic_evidence: measure/check_route.py samples the single periodic route and passes exact two-crossing projection, 34 mm crossing separation, 13.4 mm layer clearance, half-route tangent reversal, full-route tangent return, base clearance, and topological capture.
measure/check_spec.py passes rail, runner, slot/post, base, capture, and crossing-envelope inequalities against explicit minimums.

The final CAD verification pipeline regenerates from the source-only cad-source/eclipse_braid.step.py project, passes project layout and 220 mm bed fit, validates two native STEP occurrences with zero invalid parts, and reports zero clashes for the one possible occurrence pair at 1.0 mm tolerance.

The final STEP-derived STL passes watertightness, manifold edge and vertex checks, winding, positive volume, bed envelope, and 0.8 mm wall-thickness sampling; four direct views show the open frame, the two raised bridge spans, the complete route, and the captive crescent.

fit_and_print_basis.measured_clearances_mm: rail radial 1.2; post side 0.45; capture overlap 1.0 per side; runner-to-base 1.8; crossing envelope 1.4; crossing rail-center separation 13.4
fit_and_print_basis.mesh_and_wall: The final STEP-derived STL has 45,414 triangles, zero boundary edges after numerical sliver handling, zero nonmanifold edges or vertices, consistent winding, positive 15.27 cm3 volume, two expected shells, and zero sampled surface points below the 0.8 mm wall threshold.
fit_and_print_basis.print_target: One combined STEP/STL containing two intentional solids in assembly pose: one connected track/frame and one separate captive collar. No post-print assembly, hardware, adhesive, string, magnet, loose ball, or hidden support-removal feature is used.

route_family_comparison.liabilities: Requires frequent slender posts and generous moving clearances; real printed friction remains unknown until physical evaluation.
route_family_comparison.strengths: Exactly two visible alternating bridges, one uninterrupted bidirectional route, no assembly seam, no loose part, open negative space, and capture that can be checked algebraically.
route_family_comparison.topology: One closed periodic centerline with two separated projected double points and no graph vertex; a slotted collar is linked by rail-versus-post width rather than by post-print assembly.

route_family_comparison.liabilities: Adds post-print assembly, two fit-critical seams, detents, and potential runner catches; those contradict the cleaner one-piece print-in-place interpretation and add failure modes unrelated to the desired continuous motion.
route_family_comparison.strengths: Makes a one-lap orientation holonomy explicit and allows a fully closed collar.
route_family_comparison.topology: Two open rail halves joined after threading a closed collar, with accumulated section roll used to toggle a face marker.

route_family_comparison.family: Loose ball or gated transfer track
route_family_comparison.liabilities: Fails permanent capture or introduces a branch/reset action, obscures orientation, and conflicts with the Wish's exclusions.
route_family_comparison.strengths: Simple local rolling and forgiving track sections.
route_family_comparison.topology: A round loose body circulates through a branching handoff, gate, or removable closure.

selected_route_definition.capture: The collar's inner radius is 3.4 mm around a 2.2 mm rail radius. Its 2.4 mm slot is wider than a 1.5 mm support post but narrower than the 4.4 mm rail, leaving 0.45 mm post-side clearance and 1.0 mm capture overlap per rail side.
selected_route_definition.directionality_and_orientation: The route is a single periodic ordered centerline with no branch. Reversing sample order supplies the opposite travel direction. The tangent at the far lobe has dot product -1.0 with the home tangent and the tangent on return has dot product +1.0, establishing the visible mid-route reversal and home return.
selected_route_definition.layer_exchange: The low centerline is Z = 10.4 mm. A compact C1 cosine bump with 16.5 mm half-span raises the forward visit at X = -17 mm and the return visit at X = +17 mm to Z = 23.8 mm. Each crossing therefore has 13.4 mm rail-center separation and 1.4 mm envelope clearance after accounting for the runner and opposite rail.
selected_route_definition.ordered_path: The path contains 192 periodic samples: a 68 mm forward central strand, a 32-sample right half-ellipse, a 68 mm return central strand, and a 32-sample left half-ellipse. The two central strands use opposite Y cosine phases, so they project to crossings at X = -17 mm and X = +17 mm.
